ACS-5
```{r}
years <- c(2022)

state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]  

my_vars <- c(
  # Population & demographics
  tot_pop       = "B01003_001",
  median_age    = "B01002_001",
  white         = "C02003_003",
  black         = "C02003_004",
  asian         = "C02003_006",
  hispanic      = "B03001_003",

  # Economic wellbeing
  medhhinc      = "B25119_001",
  pop_poverty   = "B17001_002",
  pop_poverty_universe = "B17001_001",
  labor_force   = "B23025_003",
  unemployed    = "B23025_005",

  # Housing
  hu_ownocc     = "B25003_002",
  tot_hu        = "B25001_001",
  rent_burden_30_35   = "B25070_007",  # 30.0-34.9%
  rent_burden_35_40   = "B25070_008",  # 35.0-39.9%
  rent_burden_40_50   = "B25070_009",  # 40.0-49.9%
  rent_burden_50plus  = "B25070_010",  # 50.0%+
  rent_total          = "B25070_001",
  avg_hh_size   = "B25010_001",

  # Education
  edu_hs_or_less     = "B15003_017",
  edu_bachelors_plus = "B15003_022",
  edu_total          = "B15003_001",

  # Family structure
  divorced_m    = "B12001_010",
  divorced_f    = "B12001_019",
  single_dad_children = "B11003_010",   # male householder, no wife, with own children <18
  single_mom_children = "B11003_016" ,
# female householder, no husband, with own children <18
married_m     = "B12001_004",
  married_f     = "B12001_013"
)


census_data_tract <- map_dfr(years, function(yr) {
  map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
    get_acs(
      geography = "tract",
      variables = my_vars,
      year = yr,
      state = st,
      survey = "acs5",
      geometry = FALSE,
      cache_table = TRUE
    ) %>%
      mutate(year = yr)
  })
}) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  arrange(NAME, year)

census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(divorced = divorced_m + divorced_f,
         married  = married_m + married_f)

census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(
    divorce_rate = divorced / tot_pop * 100,
    marriage_rate = married /tot_pop * 100
  )
```

Prisons (ICPSR)
```{r}
# Prison Exposure Variables (Census Tract Level, Open Facilities, from ICPSR)
#
# Builds five spatial exposure variables at the census tract level, using only
# currently OPEN prison facilities: (1) prison_presence, a binary indicator of
# whether any open prison falls within the tract; (2) num_prisons, a count of
# open prisons within the tract; (3) dist_to_nearest_prison_mi, the distance
# in miles from the tract's own centroid to the nearest open prison nationally
# (not restricted to prisons within the tract); (4) num_prisons_within_5km, a
# count of open prisons within a 5km radius of the tract centroid; and
# (5) avg_dist_within_tract_mi, for tracts containing 1+ open prisons, the
# average distance from the tract's centroid to each of those internal
# prisons. Facility and tract polygons are centroid-reduced to points before
# any distance calculation, since points guarantee an unambiguous single
# location per unit (a full polygon-to-polygon join risks a facility matching
# more than one tract if its boundary crosses a tract line). All distances are
# computed in a projected, meters-based CRS (EPSG:5070, Albers Equal Area,
# standard for the contiguous US) rather than the source data's native
# lat/lon CRS, since distances computed directly in angular coordinates are
# distorted, especially at national scale.

# Download census tract boundaries nationwide (all 50 states + DC) 
state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]

tract_geo <- map_dfr(state_fips, function(st) {
  tracts(state = st, cb = TRUE, year = 2020)
}) %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

nrow(tract_geo)

# Load prison facilities and restrict to OPEN status only 
prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson")
prisons_icpsr <- st_make_valid(prisons_icpsr)   #repairs invalid polygon geometries before any spatial operation

prisons_open_sf <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  filter(STATUS == "OPEN")

nrow(prisons_open_sf)

#Reduce both facilities and tracts to centroid points, in a shared projected CRS
prisons_open_centroids <- st_centroid(prisons_open_sf)
prisons_open_centroids_proj <- st_transform(prisons_open_centroids, 5070)

tract_geo_proj <- st_transform(tract_geo, 5070)
tract_centroids <- st_centroid(tract_geo_proj)

# Identify which open prisons fall within which tract
# This spatial join is what attaches a tract GEOID to each individual prison,
# and must run before any tract-level summary that groups by GEOID
prisons_in_tract <- st_join(prisons_open_centroids_proj, tract_geo_proj["GEOID"], join = st_within)

#Summarize prison count, capacity, and population per tract
prisons_by_tract <- prisons_in_tract %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID)) %>%
  group_by(GEOID) %>%
  summarise(
    num_prisons    = n(),
    capacity_total = sum(CAPACITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_total      = sum(POPULATION, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Distance from each tract's centroid to the nearest open prison nationally
# Uses a nearest-neighbor search (nngeo::st_nn) 
nearest <- st_nn(tract_centroids, prisons_open_centroids_proj, k = 1, returnDist = TRUE)
tract_centroids$dist_to_nearest_prison_mi <- unlist(nearest$dist) / 1609.34   #meters -> miles

#Count of open prisons within a 5km radius of each tract centroid 
within_5km <- st_is_within_distance(tract_centroids, prisons_open_centroids_proj, dist = 5000)
tract_centroids$num_prisons_within_5km <- lengths(within_5km)

# For tracts containing 1+ open prisons, average distance from the tract's own centroid to each of those internal prisons
tracts_with_prisons <- unique(prisons_in_tract %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% filter(!is.na(GEOID)) %>% pull(GEOID))

avg_dist_within_tract <- lapply(tracts_with_prisons, function(g) {
  tract_pt <- tract_centroids %>% filter(GEOID == g)
  prisons_here <- prisons_in_tract %>% filter(GEOID == g)
  dists <- st_distance(tract_pt, prisons_here)
  tibble(GEOID = g, avg_dist_within_tract_mi = mean(as.numeric(dists)) / 1609.34)
}) %>% bind_rows()

# Assemble the final spatial dataset, joining all exposure variables back onto the full national tract layer 
tract_exposure_sf <- tract_geo_proj %>%
  left_join(prisons_by_tract, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(
    tract_centroids %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
      select(GEOID, dist_to_nearest_prison_mi, num_prisons_within_5km),
    by = "GEOID"
  ) %>%
  left_join(avg_dist_within_tract, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    num_prisons     = replace_na(num_prisons, 0),
    capacity_total  = replace_na(capacity_total, 0),
    pop_total       = replace_na(pop_total, 0),
    prison_presence = as.integer(num_prisons > 0)
  )

# Checks
nrow(tract_exposure_sf)                       
table(tract_exposure_sf$prison_presence)
summary(tract_exposure_sf$num_prisons)


```

Death counts
```{r}
#death counts and death rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm injuries by census tract of residence

injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/injury_overdose_violence_census_tract.csv")

injury_overdose_violence_exploded <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  separate_rows(NAME, sep = ",\\s*") %>%          #split combined tract lists into one row per real tract
  rename(real_tract_geoid = NAME) %>%
  mutate(real_tract_geoid = str_trim(real_tract_geoid))

# Sanity check: these should now be clean 11-digit real Census tract GEOIDs
head(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid, 10)
nchar(injury_overdose_violence_exploded$real_tract_geoid[1])

#2022
injury_overdose_violence_2022 <- injury_overdose_violence_exploded %>%
  filter(Period == "2022") %>%
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide", "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(real_tract_geoid, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME, Period),
    names_from  = Intent,
    values_from = Rate,
    names_glue  = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate,
    GEOID = real_tract_geoid,
    year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    suicide_rate  = ifelse(suicide_rate  == -999, NA, suicide_rate),
    homicide_rate = ifelse(homicide_rate == -999, NA, homicide_rate),
    overdose_rate = ifelse(overdose_rate == -999, NA, overdose_rate)
  )

nrow(injury_overdose_violence_2022)
n_distinct(injury_overdose_violence_2022$GEOID)
```

Urban vs. Rural counties (USDA)
```{r}
# Load and reshape the USDA rurality file
rural_2023 <- read_csv("data/rural_urban_codes2023.csv")  # 1-3: urban, 4-9: rural

rural_2023 <- rural_2023 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Attribute, values_from = Value) %>%
  mutate(
    Population_2020 = as.numeric(Population_2020),
    RUCC_2023 = as.numeric(RUCC_2023)
  )

rural_2023_clean <- rural_2023 %>%
  rename(county_geoid = FIPS) %>%
  mutate(rural = as.integer(RUCC_2023 >= 4))

# Drop any previously-joined rurality columns (including any .x/.y duplicates
# left over from earlier attempts), so this can be re-run safely from a messy state
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  select(-matches("^RUCC_2023(\\.[xy])?$"),
         -matches("^rural(\\.[xy])?$"),
         -matches("^Population_2020(\\.[xy])?$"))

# Derive each tract's county FIPS from its own GEOID (first 5 characters)
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  mutate(county_geoid = str_sub(GEOID, 1, 5))

# Join county-level rurality onto every tract within that county
census_data_tract <- census_data_tract %>%
  left_join(rural_2023_clean %>% select(county_geoid, RUCC_2023, rural, Population_2020),
            by = "county_geoid")

# Sanity checks
names(census_data_tract)
sum(is.na(census_data_tract$RUCC_2023))
nrow(census_data_tract)



#2013
# The 2013 Rural-Urban Continuum Codes (RUCC) from the USDA are already in wide
# format with one row per county. The only cleaning needed is renaming FIPS to GEOID
# for consistency with the join key used across all other datasets, and creating a
# binary rural indicator following the standard USDA convention where codes 1-3
# denote metro (urban) counties and codes 4-9 denote nonmetro (rural) counties.
# The 2013 vintage is used rather than 2023 because it predates the 2019 outcome
# year, which is the methodologically appropriate choice.
```

Cleaning the dataset

```{r}
# Rate/percentage variables 
master_tract <- master_tract %>%
  mutate(
    poverty_rate       = pop_poverty / pop_poverty_universe * 100,
    unemp_rate         = unemployed / labor_force * 100,
    pct_white          = white / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_black          = black / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_asian          = asian / tot_pop * 100,
    pct_hispanic       = hispanic / tot_pop * 100,
    homeown_rate       = hu_ownocc / tot_hu * 100,
    pct_bachelors_plus = edu_bachelors_plus / edu_total * 100,
    pct_hs_or_less     = edu_hs_or_less / edu_total * 100,
    rent_burdened_30plus_rate = (rent_burden_30_35 + rent_burden_35_40 + rent_burden_40_50 + rent_burden_50plus) / rent_total * 100,
    single_parent_rate = (single_dad_children + single_mom_children) / tot_hu * 100,
    pct_nonwhite = 1 - pct_white,
    log_pop            = log(tot_pop),
    log_medhhinc       = log(medhhinc),
  )

# Save
write_csv(master_tract, "data/final/tract_level_dataset_2022.csv")
```


## Analysis

```{r}
names(master_tract)
```


### OLS

### prison_presence (binary)

```{r}
d1 <- master_tract %>% filter(!is.na(overdose_rate), !is.na(prison_presence))

model1 <- lm(
  overdose_rate ~ prison_presence + pct_nonwhite + log_medhhinc + poverty_rate + unemp_rate + RUCC_2023 + pct_bachelors_plus + log_pop,
  data = d1
)

tidy(model1) %>%
  select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(term = "Term", estimate = "Estimate", std.error = "SE", statistic = "t value", p.value = "p-value") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(estimate, std.error, statistic), decimals = 4) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p.value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Overdose Rate ~ Prison Present (Binary)", subtitle = paste0("OLS, N = ", nobs(model1))) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value < 0.05)) %>%
  tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#ffe0b3"), locations = cells_body(rows = p.value >= 0.05 & p.value < 0.10))
```
